summary: Olympic lookout built in 1916, one of the first with a radio (1919); abandoned in 1930 and gone by 1947. The site is inside Olympic National Park, reached only by hard off-trail routes.

facts.status_note: Abandoned in 1930; removed or destroyed in 1947 (sources differ); no standing structure described

access.note: Inside Olympic National Park; no closure described. The routes WillhiteWeb describes are off-trail or on abandoned trails

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb: the most often attempted route is via Three Lakes and then an abandoned trail; the southern route is for experienced off-trail travelers only

events.note: Log cabin built by the U.S. Forest Service
One of the first lookouts outfitted with a radio to report fires
Mavie Olsen (also spelled Olson) appointed lookout, per a July 30, 1920 Mason County Journal report
New wireless station at the lookout, per a July 4, 1921 newspaper report
Edwin Wilson in charge of the station's radio observation post, per a June 30, 1932 Centralia newspaper report; WillhiteWeb's narrative places him there in 1921, but the dated quote is 1932
The register says removed; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says removed in 1947; firelookout.com and WillhiteWeb say destroyed in 1947. All three agree the cabin is gone.
The 1920 appointee is spelled Olsen in the Mason County Journal report and Olson in WillhiteWeb's profile of her
Olympic National Forest in 1920 (newspaper headers); the site is in Olympic National Park and administered by the National Park Service today
The register gives 3,419 ft (1,042 m), which matches the record's 1042.1 m. firelookout.com says 3400' and WillhiteWeb says 3,376 feet

notes_for_editor: The shared WebSearch budget ran out before this tower's search, so the story rests only on the four cached pages listed. The 1920, 1921 and 1932 staffing and radio facts come from newspaper excerpts quoted on the Forest Lookouts and WillhiteWeb pages; the original newspapers were not checked. The 1947 fate is in dispute (removed vs destroyed) and is recorded as 'removed' with the disagreement noted. No photos added: licences not checked. Olympic National Park's current backcountry rules were not checked.
